reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through Nov 20: SPX 6,910.39, -11.91% from its 120-day high, -9.37% below its 50-day and -5.96% below its 200-day; SMH -40.45% and NVDA -48.42% from their highs, both BELOW Zone 2; VIX 35.89 at its 5-day high; HY OAS 3.52 with credit still calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4. Data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: SPX reclaims its 50-day (7,625.26) and SMH/NVDA reclaim and hold Zone 2 (470-505 / 175-185) with the mechanical tally moving to 3 of 4 — that would prove the Watch stance too cautious and void the ladder's escalation rungs.

ladder.response: Escalation confirmed: stay in Watch, no probes; re-price the next zone down and wait for the failed-bounce/second-low sequence before any deployment.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below 6,900 or SMH closes below $380 (a further leg down from $400.06)

ladder.response: Bull-trap case: do not chase the bounce; treat the failure as confirmation the correction is not over, and any staged selling happens on that strength, never after a break.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the failure zone 7,750-7,820 or SMH into 580-600 and fails there

ladder.response: Stand-down / regime-break conditions met: deployment ladder frozen, all tranche triggers void until credit calms and a confirmed bottom forms.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS crosses 4.00% or SPX closes a second week below 7,000 with no bounce

ladder.response: Re-entry condition: move to Probe per the deployment ladder (Tranche A: Zone 2 prints plus tally at least 3 of 6), sized small, with the zone floor as the invalidation.
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds, with the 10-year falling, or SMH/NVDA reclaim Zone 2 (470-505 / 175-185) and hold with VIX rolling over from 35.89

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the base risk this week: the first bounce has not even formed, and when it does, TQQQ/CONL will rip hardest and look like leadership. Entries do not chase a single green day or a levered bounce; they wait for the failure-zone retest verdict (SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600) or a second low that holds. A bounce that fails at the zone is the trap — it resets the clock, it does not arm a buy.

strategyPosture: Watch. No tranche is armed: the AI complex sits below its buy zones, the capitulation tally is 1 of 4, and there has not yet been a first bounce — prepare the ladder and size nothing into the tape.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: credit conditions can flip, and a 13-point leadership gap with NVDA at -48.4% is the shape a rollover takes before it broadens. The rotation read holds only while credit stays calm — if HY OAS crosses 4.00%, the classification flips.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 11.7% below its 52-week high, a 13.27-point gap to the Mag7 average — the weakness is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, not spread across it. Credit confirms the read: bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.52%, still calm and below the 4.00% stand-down line.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag7 collapse, index holding
themes.narrative: The Mag7-led selloff reads as a broad market rollover: the average Mag7 name sits 24.97% below its 52-week high, with NVDA the weakest at -48.4%, and the tape feels like indiscriminate liquidation.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.00% or the Mag7-SPY gap widening while SPY's distance from its high closes toward the Mag7 average.

themes.counterRead: Cheap on growth is not a bottom: SMH and NVDA both sit BELOW Zone 2 (SMH $400.06 vs Zone 2 $470-505; NVDA $125.53 vs Zone 2 $175-185), the mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4, VIX is at its 5-day high of 35.89, and there has not yet been a first bounce. The setup is the widest in the market, but the entry trigger has not fired — buying into the fall is catching a knife, not buying the gap.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue is still growing fast while prices collapse: NVDA revenue +61.4% YoY at $125.53, -48.4% from its high with RSI 15; AVGO +55% YoY, -38.5% from its high; LRCX +131.3% YoY, -58.2% from its high; ONTO +41.5% YoY with $300M FCF (29.8% FCF margin), -56% from its high; DDOG +27.7% YoY with 80% gross margin, -47.7% from its high. The dislocation list classifies 38 names as sentiment-driven declines, not earnings-driven ones, and the top-conviction screen scores ONTO 85, DDOG 84, AVGO 83 — all on revenue growth against price collapse.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is finished — NVDA down 14.01% in a day, SMH down 10.6%, and the whole complex 40-60% off its highs, so the market has priced the AI buildout as a bust.
themes.watchFor: SMH reclaiming Zone 2 ($470-505) and NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 ($175-185) and holding, with the capitulation tally moving to 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: Credit is a lagging confirmer, not a leading all-clear: spreads can gap fast if the equity drawdown deepens into a second leg, so the calm is a condition to monitor, not a floor to trust. The stand-down line is 4.00%; 48 basis points of room is not a wide margin.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit has not cracked: HY OAS is 3.52%, the episode block marks credit 'calm: true, cracking: false', and it is the only confirmed signal in the 1-of-4 mechanical tally. The curve is not inverted (2s10s +0.28), the real 10-year is 2.89%, and lending standards are loose at 1.7%. The stress is in equity prices — SPX -8.61% in five sessions, QQQ -10.54% in a month — not in funding markets.
themes.label: Credit calm, equity panic — the stress narrative runs ahead of the data
themes.narrative: VIX at 35.89, up 26.2% in a day and 86% in five days, with the 10-year at 5.04% and the 2-year at 4.76%, says the market is pricing a credit event alongside the equity drawdown.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.00%, or a second consecutive week of SPX below 7,000 with no bounce.

themes.counterRead: The trap is reading the levered bounce as the bottom: when the first bounce comes, TQQQ and CONL will rip hardest and look like leadership, but a bounce into the failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820) that fails is the bull-trap case. Levered names stay off the buy list until the mechanical tally confirms — a green day in TQQQ proves nothing about the episode.
themes.dataAnchor: These are the deepest 1-month losses in the entire 40-symbol universe, and the pattern is mechanical: SPX is -11.91% from its 120-day high, so a 3x levered vehicle losing a third of its value in a month is arithmetic, not a new signal. Holdings carry the same damage directly — TQQQ -8.26% on the day, CONL -5.59%, BMNR -36.71% in a month — while the unlevered index is down far less.
themes.label: Levered tail wipeout — the damage concentrates where leverage lives
themes.narrative: The leveraged and crypto-linked complex has been destroyed — CONL -63.1% in a month, TQQQ -32.31%, BTC -20.04%, ETH -23.32%, DOGE -24.83% — and the market treats that as proof the whole risk apparatus is broken.
themes.watchFor: Any first bounce in TQQQ/CONL that reaches the SPX failure zone (7,750-7,820) and whether it holds or fails there.
